root_idea.summary: The evidence presents two principal axes: the arāk tree and remaining or settling in a place.
root_idea.development: The tree axis extends to grazing, arāk-rich land, camel descriptions, and dense or mature growth. The abiding axis extends to staying, persistence, withdrawal, compulsion, and the couch term أَرِيكَةٌ, explained through a place of abode or association with arāk wood.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic form is the plural أَرَائِكُ; the public headword is normalized to its supported singular dictionary citation form أَرِيكَةٌ.

senses.definition: A raised, ornamentally furnished couch or reclining seat.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran occurrences use the plural أَرَائِكُ for elevated furnished seats or couches on which people recline. Contextual renderings may vary between “couches” and “thrones” without requiring separate lexical senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, continue, or abide in a place, especially among trees while feeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The broader use may describe a person remaining in a place, or camels remaining among arāk or other trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist or persevere in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical extension of remaining or continuing, used with an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold back or draw back in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported tropical use distinct from persistence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed camels upon arāk, or to make them feed or remain among such trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I construction involving camels and arāk trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel or constrain someone to undertake an affair, or to make that person keep or cleave to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive tropical construction with a person and an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to suffer a belly complaint or pain caused by eating arāk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated adjective also describes camels affected in this way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To conceal someone by means of an أَرِيكَةٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; the construction refers to concealment using a couch, canopy, or curtained enclosure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of arāk, to become firm, strong, compact, mature, tangled, luxuriant, or abundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII, used of the arāk tree or its growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage in which camels remain or continue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for grazing vegetation associated with camels’ remaining there.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The arāk tree, a known thorny tree with bunch-like fruit and abundant branches.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its branches and roots are used for tooth-cleaning; the term can also describe abundant, tangled, or luxuriant arāk growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land or a piece of ground abounding in arāk trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive expression for arāk-rich terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that feed upon arāk or remain among such trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is also associated with the plural form أَوَارِكُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A people or company who alight and abide by arāk trees while feeding their camels there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive participial expression for people settled by arāk trees in connection with camel grazing.

cautions: The Quranic public headword is normalized to singular أَرِيكَةٌ, while all five supplied Quran occurrences are inflected plural forms أَرَائِكُ.
The Lane citation to “xviii. 30” is retained only as historical lexical evidence and is not converted into a modern verse location; the examples use the independently supplied QAC locations.
The supplied contextual renderings vary between couches and thrones; this variation does not by itself establish an additional sense.
